newsitem.title: USA: 3D Systems says Q1 will not meet views.
newsitem.headline: 3D Systems says Q1 will not meet views.

text.p: 3D Systems Corp said Friday its first quarter earnings will not meet analysts' estimates, though the company does expect to be profitable in the quarter.
Analysts predict earnings of $0.10 per share, flat with the company's 1996 first quarter, according to First Call.
Results will be announced on April 24, 3D said.

The company also said Richard Balanson has been elected president and chief operating officer, succeeding Charles Hull, the company's founder, who assumes the newly-created posts of vice chairman and chief technology officer.

Balanson, 47, who joined the company last November, will head manufacturing, product development, worldwide field service and international sales, reporting to Arthur Sims, chairman and chief executive officer, the company said.
Balanson was also elected to the company's board of directors, the company said.

Gordon Almquist, vice president, finance and chief financial officer, and Richard Fedchenko, vice president, strategy and market development, have resigned to pursue other interests, the company said.

Edward Ferrier, the company's corporate controller, has been named acting chief financial officer, and on an interim basis U.S. marketing will be under the direct supervision of Sims, the company said.
